summary: HP ZBook EC firmware update disables NVMe hotplug when docked, causing SCCM task sequence hang during provisioning
description:
Issue summary:
During routine depot returns we observed a cluster of HP ZBook/EliteBook devices failing to complete SCCM task sequences. Devices hit a hard hang at 'Apply Operating System' (TS step 5) when docked to the HP USB-C docking station. Investigation shows the Embedded Controller (EC) firmware that was applied during depot repair disables NVMe hotplug/enumeration while a dock is attached. This results in the NVMe drive not being visible to the Windows PE environment and the Task Sequence stalls.

Impact:
- Blocks provisioning of devices returned to depot (affects ~18 units across the last 3 days).
- Prevents reimaging of laptops in depot workflows; delays RMA turn-around and staging for new hires.
- Workstation provisioning pipelines are impacted in us-west provisioning racks when docks are present.

Environment details:
- SCCM (ConfigMgr) task sequence v2209 running WinPE 10.0.19041.
- Devices built by depot 2024-11 (EC firmware v1.02.04).
- Dock used: HP USB-C G5 Docking Station (firmware unknown).

Observed behavior / error state:
- WinPE fails to see NVMe device, diskpart "list disk" shows no disk.
- BIOS/UEFI shows NVMe present when booted natively (without dock) but disappears when dock connected.
- Device logs: "StorPort: NVMe controller not present after PCIe reset" entries in WinPE logs when docked.
- No SCCM/TS error code returned (TS hung on disk step, status 0x0).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Take an HP ZBook Firefly G9 with depot EC firmware v1.02.04 and attach HP USB-C dock.
2) PXE boot the device into corporate WinPE / SCCM task sequence (same TS used for imaging).
3) Observe SCCM TS stall at 'Apply Operating System' as WinPE 'diskpart list disk' shows no drives.
4) Remove dock, reboot to WinPE; disk becomes visible and TS resumes/completes normally.
logs: WinPE storport snippet: [storport] NVMe controller 0000:05:00.0 not found after reset (rc=0x12)
UEFI event: EC reported "PCIe lane power save engaged" when dock attached; NVMe BAR disabled
SCCM TS: no error code; currently recorded as 'Task Sequence timeout' in SCCM server logs
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: EC firmware introduces a new power management policy that disables NVMe when an alternate Thunderbolt/USB-C host controller is present. This causes WinPE to see no storage device while dock is attached.
Hypothesis 2: Dock's firmware interacts with EC over I2C leading to PCIe port gating; change in EC firmware made behavior more aggressive post-repair.
Reproduction verified on 3/3 returned units when dock is present; 0/3 when dock removed. Repro is deterministic in lab.
Captured UEFI logs from one unit and packaged driver/UEFI traces for HP support (see related_confluence_pages runbook attachment link).
comments: Asha Menon (2024-11-15): Opened after depot reported 12 units unable to reprovision; initial triage points to EC firmware applied during repair wave 2024-11-10.
Liam Rodriguez (2024-11-16): Reproduced in lab with HP G5 dock. Repro steps added. Will escalate to HP firmware support and open case. Assigned to depot lead to hold affected units.
Depot Tech - Maria Gutierrez (2024-11-16): Quarantine list created; we are pulling all ZBooks repaired since 2024-11-08 for manual inspection.
Liam Rodriguez (2024-11-17): Created escalation package (UEFI + storport logs + reproduction guide). Filed ticket with HP (case #HP-CL-78432). Awaiting response.
mitigation: 1) Immediate workaround: instruct depot technicians to remove USB-C/Thunderbolt docks prior to running SCCM task sequence. This allows imaging to complete.
2) Temporarily hold all ZBook/EliteBook devices with EC firmware v1.02.04 until HP provides guidance.
3) Update depot runbook: add pre-imaging checklist to ensure no docks attached and to validate disk visibility in WinPE before running full TS.
resolution: In progress: Active engagement with HP firmware team (case HP-CL-78432). Temporary mitigation implemented in depot runbook (remove dock prior to imaging). Next steps: receive HP repro fix or EC rollback instructions; if HP provides non-destructive EC rollback, depot team will apply and run 10-device validation before clearing hold. Follow-up: add automated WinPE disk visibility check to SCCM TS to surface this class of failure earlier.
root_cause: Under investigation — suspected EC firmware power-management change introduced in depot repair image that disables NVMe PCIe BAR when an alternate controller (dock) is attached. Awaiting vendor confirmation.
next_steps: Await HP response with firmware analysis (owner: Liam Rodriguez).
If HP supplies EC rollback or patch, test on 5 units in staging and validate with SCCM TS (owner: Depot Lead).
Add a WinPE pre-check step to SCCM task sequence to detect missing disks and fail fast with a clear diagnostic ticket for depot technicians (owner: Imaging SRE).
